newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada deficit to be gone by 1999/2000 - Liberals.
newsitem.headline: Canada deficit to be gone by 1999/2000 - Liberals.

text.p: Canada's Liberal government, campaigning for re-election, is predicting that the country's budget deficit will be eliminated within two years.
Prime Minister Jean Chretien made the prediction on Thursday while on the campaign trail for the June 2 election, a party spokesman said on Friday.
"It looks reasonable at this point from where we stand that the deficit will probably be gone in two years," Sean Kirby said in a phone interview.

"What we've done for the last four years is to set new targets every two years," he said. "Obviously, we are well ahead of where we have targeted in each of the last budget years. And from where we stand at this point, it looks like we're going to be down to a zero deficit for 1999-2000."

The government originally predicted a deficit for 1996-97 of C$24.3 billion. But the Finance Department revised its estimate in February to C$19 billion and said last week it would come in under C$16 billion.
The Prime Minister has suggested the final figure for the year could be as low as C$15 billion.
